speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Under the Act, the TCMP Board, or referred to as "the Board", was established to register practitioners engaging in prescribed practices of TCM in Singapore, accredit TCM courses for the purpose of registration as well as the Singapore institutions of higher learning (IHLs) offering such courses, regulate the professional conduct and ethics of registered practitioners, and make recommendations on the continuing training and education of registered practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Since then, the Ministry of Health (MOH) and the Board have progressively put in place programmes and frameworks to raise the professional standards of TCMPs in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Last year, a $5 million TCM Development Grant was also established to support skills development and capability-building of the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Individual TCMPs are eligible to apply for the Development Grant, capped at $200 per year, to defray the cost of attending TCM classes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Accredited TCM training providers may also seek funding support to conduct local TCM conferences and seminars.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As we strengthen professionalism within the TCM sector, MOH has reviewed the Act to ensure that the Act remains relevant and responsive towards the changing practice environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The TCMP (Amendment) Bill before us today proposes amendments to the Act to better protect patients' interests and safety, improve the timeliness and fairness of the disciplinary framework for registered TCMPs, and help raise professional standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Speaker, allow me now to highlight the major provisions of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Continuing professional learning is important to ensure that TCMPs keep themselves current in their professional practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Continuing professional education (CPE) has already been implemented for other healthcare professions, such as doctors, nurses and pharmacists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH and the Board introduced voluntary CPE in 2013 to enhance the standards and safety of TCM practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Under the voluntary CPE programme, all registered TCMPs are encouraged to accumulate at least 25 CPE points per year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 5 of the Bill amends section 17 of the Act to provide that the Board may refuse to grant or renew a Practising Certificate (PC) if the TCMP fails to comply with the prescribed CPE requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The requirement, as defined, would allow some flexibility for individuals to plan their learning without unduly affecting their professional practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We developed this CPE points assessment framework after engaging with the TCM community extensively on CPE since 2013, taking note of their concerns on the availability and the range of CPE courses offered and the reasonableness of the costs of these courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We appreciate the constructive feedback and have taken them into consideration, such as expanding the accredited course offerings to include new modes of learning to suit the different needs of TCMPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Currently, all complaints against registered TCMPs are investigated by Investigation Committees appointed by the Board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: While these cover a wide range of matters, the disciplinary framework does not adequately deal with allegations that a registered TCMP is unfit to practise due to his physical or mental condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These cases do require a different approach since a health inquiry into the TCMP's fitness to practise is required, as opposed to an investigation into an incident or transaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The current framework also does not enable stoppage orders to be made in extreme situations where a TCMP must be made to immediately stop practising because of serious and imminent risk to the public if there is no stoppage, or if stoppage is required to avoid any actual incident that endangers the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 11 of the Bill introduces the new Part IVA of the Act, which sets out the revised disciplinary framework for TCMPs, which I will elaborate next in detail.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: First, the new section 26A allows a registered TCMP to voluntarily curtail his practice if he believes that (a) his fitness to practise is impaired by his physical or mental condition; or (b) the quality of the professional services he provides does not meet the standard which it is reasonable to expect of a registered TCMP to carry out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Board, with the agreement of the registered TCMP, may cancel the practitioner’s registration, suspend the registration for up to three years or impose appropriate conditions on the registration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: A disciplinary inquiry does not need to be conducted in order for the Board to accede to the practitioner’s request.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, this avenue will not be available in cases where there is evidence of professional misconduct or there is a pending disciplinary inquiry against the practitioner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The process in the new section 26A is initiated by the TCMP himself or herself, which encourages practitioners to come forward if they are of the view that they are unable to continue practising at the standard expected of a registered TCMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This improves the timeliness of the process and allows the Board to resolve appropriate cases expeditiously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Second, the new Part IVA sets out in the body of the amended Act a revised framework for inquiries into disciplinary matters concerning a registered TCMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The processes have been streamlined to speed things up and to fit the introduction of a health inquiry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: A person may make a complaint against, or provide information about, any registered TCMP to the Board touching on any of the grounds set out in section 19(1).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The complaint or information will be reviewed by the Board upon receipt, and for purposes of its review, the Board may require the complainant or TCMP concerned to answer any inquiry or provide any record that the Board considers relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Board may dismiss any complaint or information that is frivolous, vexatious, misconceived or lacking in substance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, if the case is not dismissed on any of those grounds, the Board must refer the complaint to an Inquiry Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Inquiry Committee must direct one or more investigators to investigate the facts and circumstances of the complaint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The investigator must give the TCMP concerned written notice of the complaint against him, and the TCMP can provide a written explanation to the investigator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The TCMP will also have the opportunity to appear before the Inquiry Committee, whether in person or represented by counsel, to be heard on the complaint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Upon completion of its inquiry, the Inquiry Committee will submit a report of its findings to the Board, together with its recommendations on the disciplinary action to be taken under section 19 of the Act against the TCMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: After considering the Inquiry Committee's report, the Board may take such action under section 19 as it thinks fit or dismiss the case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In appropriate cases, the Board may also refer the complaint back to the Inquiry Committee once more for the Inquiry Committee’s reconsideration or a further report on such matters as the Board may specify.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: No prior inquiry or investigation is needed before making such an interim order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: But the Board may do so only if there are reasonable grounds to believe that, either there is a serious and imminent risk to the public if there is no such stoppage, or if it is to avoid any actual incident that endangers the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: If the Board is satisfied that it continues to be necessary to prevent the TCMP from practising, the Board may confirm the interim order, with or without modifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Before the interim order is confirmed, the Board must refer the interim order to an Inquiry Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The TCMP may make representations or objections against the proposed confirmation to the Inquiry Committee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Inquiry Committee will then consider the facts of the case before making a recommendation to the Board whether or not to confirm the interim order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The next group of amendments concerns the disciplinary penalties that may be imposed on a registered TCMP who has been found guilty following a disciplinary inquiry under the new Part IVA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Currently, the Board may cancel the registration of an errant TCMP if he has been found guilty of professional misconduct or negligence, or any of the other grounds of misconduct under section 19 of the Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The increase will bring about better alignment with the other healthcare professional Acts and provide greater assurance and confidence to the public that errant TCMPs will be dealt with appropriately as against other healthcare practitioners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 7(d) introduces further disciplinary penalties that the Board may impose on the TCMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These include the Board ordering the errant TCMP to give an undertaking, on such terms as the Board thinks fit, to abstain from the conduct that was the subject of the disciplinary inquiry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Board may also refer the matter for mediation between the TCMP and the complainant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Examples of cases that may be suited for mediation include cases arising from poor service provided to patients and miscommunication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Taking clauses 7(h) and 9 of the Bill together, sections 19(5) and 21 provide that the Board's decisions on disciplinary matters does not take effect until the thirty-first day after the date of the decision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is to allow the TCMP sufficient time to consider whether to file an appeal to the High Court against the Board's decision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Similar provisions are found in the Medical Registration Act and the Pharmacists Registration Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 12 of the Bill repeals and re-enacts sections 28 to 30 of the Act to enhance the enforcement powers of investigators investigating into disciplinary matters concerning registered TCMPs, as well as offences under the Act, such as unlawful practice of TCM by unregistered persons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Currently, for the purpose of investigating into offences under the Act, authorised officers may enter and inspect any premises which are used or suspected to be used to carry out any prescribed practice of TCM and inquire into the conditions under which the practice is carried out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, the officers are unable to search the premises or seize evidence without a warrant, which hinders the timely and effective conduct of investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, if the investigator is investigating into a disciplinary complaint under the new Part IVA, these powers of entry, search and seizure can be exercised only if (a) a Court warrant has been obtained; (b) the occupier of the place consents; or (c) the investigator believes on reasonable grounds that there is an imminent or immediate danger of serious bodily injury or death to any individual who is receiving or who is about to receive any treatment at the place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The new section 30 makes it an offence for a person to (a) provide any document or give information that is false or misleading in a material particular; (b) knowingly obstruct or prevent an investigator in the discharge of the investigator's powers or duties; (c) intentionally alter, suppress or destroy any document or information which the person is required to provide; or (d) fail, without reasonable excuse, to provide any information the person is required to provide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Next, I will turn to the other amendments in the Bill, which are mostly of a housekeeping nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Taking in feedback from the TCM community, clause 3 of the Bill amends section 3(2) of the Act to increase the maximum size of the Board from nine to 11 members, which allows for a broader representation of the TCM profession on the Board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 6 repeals and re-enacts section 18 so that the Registrar of the Board is not constrained in publishing a list containing information about all registered TCMPs with a valid practising certificate in the Gazette.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Instead, the amendment will allow the list to be published on the Board's website or by other means.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 8 amends section 20 to clarify the types of costs and expenses that the Board may require a TCMP who is the subject of disciplinary proceedings under Part IVA to pay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This includes the cost and expenses of any assessor or advocate and solicitor appointed by the Board for any proceedings before an Inquiry Committee, and reasonable expenses the Board may pay to witnesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 14 inserts a new section 34A to provide that the Board may compound any offence under the Act that is prescribed as a compoundable offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This empowers the Board to compound such offences without having to rely on section 243 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: (In Mandarin):   The upholding of practice standards of TCMPs is important as the TCM profession matures and develops in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Therefore, MOH values and encourages the continuing education of TCMPs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have successfully introduced voluntary CPEs in 2013 and received positive feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: After the passage of this Bill, it will, indeed, be a milestone for the TCM community as we implement compulsory CPE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are grateful for the feedback from the community on the implementation of CPE and have also taken in their feedback, such as expanding the learning platforms to include accredited online courses, and to award more points for instructors and self-learners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Besides CPE, MOH also hopes to enhance the regulatory regime by amending the Bill to further strengthen the disciplinary framework for greater efficiency and to maintain public and patient safety more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: (In English): With this, I seek Members' support for this Bill.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In recent years, both our Prime Minister and our Minister for Health have remarked on the critical role that TCM can play in improving the health of our citizens, particularly within the context of an ageing population.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I, too, would like to put on record my appreciation to the TCM community for the contributions to Singapore's healthcare.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Certainly, TCM remains a medical remedy of choice for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The amendments to this Act, which was first passed in 2000, are timely and vital for the TCM sector to grow and achieve its true potential in providing for the healthcare needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have three comments and clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, the clarifications to the disciplinary framework are welcome and will certainly improve self-regulation within the TCM sector and increase public trust.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For instance, how robust will the renamed Inquiry Committee's decision regarding a practitioner's physical or mental fitness to practise be?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a challenge that western medicine is also facing.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For instance, in the United States (US), there was a much discussed case or incident where a senior surgeon in his early 70s, while supervising a procedure, fell asleep during the surgery.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This particular surgeon was not performing the surgery itself, but concerns were raised.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And there were many discussions between the Board of the hospital and various communities.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But the problem they faced was that it was difficult to prove fitness or unfitness from a mental or physical point of view.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Just by going by normal physical and mental tests alone, he passed.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The case was finally resolved by the voluntary withdrawal of the physician in question from clinical practice.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But these are challenges that have no easy answers.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would just like to find out, with this Inquiry Committee, how will it deal with such cases?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What would be considered an acceptable treatment modality and what would not be considered an acceptable treatment modality, considering that TCM embraces a wide range of treatment philosophies and modalities, some of which may be at odds with one another?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope that the Ministry will be able to elaborate on how the procedural aspects of these disciplinary processes can be made more robust and better able to stand up to scrutiny, with these amendments.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If these inactive practitioners do not participate in the CPE programme and do not practise, will this affect them if they decide to re-enter active practice in the future and reapply for a PC or licence?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Third, I note also that the maximum number of members of the TCM Board will increase from nine to 11 under the proposed amendments.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: The enhancement of professional standards that this Bill aims to bring about is welcomed.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: It follows that effective regulatory regimes would not be the same for both.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: However, western medicine constitutes the mainstream of modern medicine and healthcare and has relatively comprehensive professional training and regulatory frameworks worthy of learning from.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: I hope we can lengthen our stride and quicken our pace in this direction, the better to make our contributions in bringing more benefits of TCM to the world.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: I hope that TCM remedies which have proven to be effective and safe following thorough clinical experimentation can be integrated into our healthcare system without delay for the benefit of more patients.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: At such point, the Government may adopt complementary measures so that TCM may be more widely available to all, such as the increased scope for payment in MediSave funds for TCM items, the provision of subsidies for TCM treatment under CHAS or PG), or the recognition of MCs issued by TCMPs.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This could be due to the increased demand for alternative therapies, an enhanced awareness for such therapies and also the fact that there are now more interest and research into this area.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: When we speak of TCM, it can conjure different images in different persons, ranging from the neighbourhood sinseh shops with herbal smells, to the very established companies, such as Eu Yang Sang International Ltd.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: There are always certain code of conduct, etiquette and practice guidelines which will be ascribed to every body of professionals.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The same must apply to TCMPs, who are also involved in caring for the public and patients and thus must be assessed with accountability as well.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Since then, have there been any cases which required disciplinary action or suspension?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: If so, what are the common reasons or root causes?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I ask about this with an intent to see if we can address some of these in this latest Bill that we are discussing today.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This way, we can appoint the appropriate type of TCM personnel or even specialists to provide opinion and consultation or serve as an expert witness.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I also have a few suggestions to make.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: One, to have the setup of a directory electronically for courses and training being offered for easy access and knowledge of all TCMPs.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The usual organisers can come together to discuss and brainstorm this and see how best to execute.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But for those who want to offer ad hoc courses and training, there should be a body of persons looking into the suitability of these courses to ensure certain standards are met.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: There must be a secretariat to also monitor and carry out surveillance to track the number of points and warn practitioners of the shortfall if they risk not getting renewal of their PCs.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: There were some concerns on the cost to be borne by the practitioners themselves for these courses.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: In the Medical and Nursing profession, for example, established institutions have got a sponsorship scheme and other forms of support for their practitioners.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: For large TCM groups, this may be feasible to offer.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But for the lone TCMP, there may need to be other considerations given or offer of subsidies or, perhaps, even accreditation scheme.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This will be for the Ministry to review and consider.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Of course, some courses can be offered online, though e-learning will also take time and money to set up.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Some offset can take place by offering some of these courses through SkillsFuture or other upgrading grants.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But that is something to be reviewed with caution.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can I ask if there will be some flexibility given to the TCMPs, especially for the first two years as the running-in period?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This request is with the consideration that some of our TCMPs are in the older generation and they are in solo practices and they may need time to adjust to this, to get used to the new guidelines as well.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Next, can I get some clarification on the term "TCM practitioner" as used in this Bill?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are the people who run the sinseh shops, prescribing herbal type medications in this category as well?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How about those who offer massage and tuina services as practitioners as well as the dispensers in the neighbourhood shops?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are they also incorporated into this Bill under consideration?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: On the 11 members of the Board, can I suggest also that they represent TCMPs who are generalists and also some who are specialists in certain aspects of the practice?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But I also note that we may need to have the relevant and adequate numbers of specialists in the TCM area for now, so, therefore, this is something perhaps to be considered later on.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With TCM services, the fees, we note can range from as low as $1 to $2 in the neighbourhood and community clinics to the highly priced ones in advanced centres.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Will we be moving towards some range standardisation, perhaps even into different categories of services which are being offered?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are we planning to come up with some standardisation or guidelines?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I think it will continue to be because of the range of services as well as the TCMPs that are out there.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: So, perhaps some comment from the Ministry on this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In recent years, TCM has become more popular as a career of choice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: From 2012 to 2017, the number of practitioners rose by 16%.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, as the profession swells in ranks, it must keep up its standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the growth in numbers, degree holders still comprise only 21% of all registered practitioners, according to 2017 data.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some 5.7% of practitioners have no formal qualifications at all.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Practitioners must continue to learn, unlearn and relearn to keep up with the times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, it clarifies and elaborates the mechanisms used to keep practitioners in check.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I agree with these measures, and I thank MOH for holding a public consultation and incorporating views from that consultation into this piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have five points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In effect, we are saying that Western physicians get fined $100,000 for doing wrong, while TCM physicians get fined $50,000 for doing wrong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In its response to the public consultation, the Ministry said that the Medical Registration Act more seriously penalises Western physicians for one reason only – that they pose "greater risk of potential harm to patients".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister explain how a Western physician might be more dangerous than a TCMP?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The physician conveyed a whole slew of dangerous advice to his patient.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He told her that the tumor would grow slowly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He told her that surgery would make the cancer cells proliferate more quickly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He told her that her tumor was not life-threatening.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, he prescribed capsules of ginseng and herb that, at best, provided a false sense of comfort for his patient.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were lucky that the patient’s daughter interceded and that the patient went ahead, promptly, with surgery.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am concerned about the message that this difference in fines sends.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When patients sit in a physician’s office, the physician is the figure of authority.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: TCM physicians are in a prime position to influence the health decisions of patients.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this case, the physician took the patient down a dangerous, life-threatening course of action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I urge the Ministry to further explain why a TCMP should face a less severe penalty than a Western medical practitioner.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am heartened that the Bill empowers the TCM Practitioners Board to reject the registration of practitioners who fail to comply with requirements on mandatory professional education.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My question is whether the Board can issue such requirements as part of a punishment imposed on errant practitioners.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the case I previously mentioned, the Board issued only a fine and a suspension to the practitioner even though it found that he was "neither remorseful for his conduct nor fully aware of the danger that he posed to that patient." From that statement, it appears the practitioner did not agree or understand that what he did was wrong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What then is stopping him from making similar mistakes of the same nature when he returns to practice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What course of action has been taken to ensure his knowledge base is updated to what the profession demands?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In many industries, it is common for errant professionals to undergo some programme of training or education to rectify their gap in knowledge and understanding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Ministry clarify whether the TCM Practitioners Act equips the Board with powers to require offending practitioners to undergo specific courses of professional training?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third point is about responding to complainants.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 26E details an array of timelines.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Upon receiving a complaint, the Board has two weeks to start a review and three months to complete that review.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If they refer the matter to an Inquiry Committee, the committee has six months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All in all, it seems that the process can take just under a year, extensions notwithstanding.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a long time for a complainant to wait.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My questions are as follows: does the Board have an obligation to respond to the complainant with the results of its review?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the review proceeds to the stage where an Inquiry Committee is convened to investigate, must the complainant be notified about the final findings?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In either case, is there a requirement that the Board relays information in any prompt manner to the complainant?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is laudable that we have an extensive framework for investigating complaints.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Surely, the point of these investigations is not only to be accountable but also to demonstrate accountability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It then seems important to me that the Board has a duty to reply to the complainant in a reasonably prompt fashion with a response that meaningfully addresses the complainant's concerns.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My fourth point is about sharing the results of investigations with former patients.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If TCM physicians have conducted themselves in a dangerous way, it is possible that they have done it before.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, a physician who has given incorrect advice about how to deal with cancer might well have said similar things to other cancer patients.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The TCM Practitioners Act does not appear to mandate that the Board release investigation results to former patients of the errant physician.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Historically, we have seen some cases of misconduct by TCM practitioners reported in the news media.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, it is perhaps not a stretch to say that many TCM patients may not follow the news media closely.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thus, they may not be aware that the diagnosis or treatment they received was shoddy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My fifth and last point relates to mental and physical condition.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 6 of the Act bars a person from membership of the board if "he is incapacitated by a mental or physical disability." Section 19 contains a similar phrase.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, why does one use "disability" while the other use "condition"?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Does the Ministry mean to make a meaningful distinction between the two usages?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: More specifically, what would be a condition or disability that results in incapacity or inability to carry out safe and effective practice?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is a certifying doctor, Western or TCM, required to weigh in?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Clarifications on this point, I believe, will provide guidance in future when there is any such dispute.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It reflects meaningful input solicited through the Ministry's public consultation, and it provides a robust framework with which to regulate a profession that helps manage the health of many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, I welcome it as it will help to raise the standard of professionalism in this sector and increase public confidence in TCM.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many of our elderly across different ethnic groups have been relying on TCM or a combination of TCM and Western medical treatments.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: TCM has made significant contributions to public healthcare in our multiracial society.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is also gaining recognition and popularity in the West.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am convinced that it is also beneficial for the TCMPs to be kept updated about the new findings, best practices and latest technologies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such a move is necessary for the protection of patients and will also increase the confidence of patients in TCM professionals.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The reputation and image of the TCM sector will also be lifted by enhanced professionalism and higher standards as a result.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instances where there had been complaints about negligence or misconduct not directly related to the treatment aspects, will there be an avenue for mediation?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, what efforts have been made to accord the accreditation to "Tie Da" physicians?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to know how many patients have used TCM services each year for the past 10 years.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Mandarin):   Deputy Speaker, Sir, MOH is working together with top TCM organisations to provide continual training for TCMPs, which will benefit both the practitioners and the patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: TCMPs will be able to learn the most up-to-date, advanced professional knowledge and medical treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: By doing so, Singapore can become another world-class regional medical hub.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Mr Louis Ng highlighted the increasing popularity of TCM and the growing number of registered TCMPs in Singapore, and hence the need for a robust regulatory and disciplinary framework and a code of conduct, etiquette and practice guidelines for TCMPs to provide greater assurance and confidence to the public.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members have also expressed support for the implementation of compulsory CPE to raise the standards of the profession.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef asked if subsidies could be offered to TCMPs to defray the costs of attending CPE courses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is in addition to the $90,000 granted to accredited TCM training providers for the organisation of TCM conferences and seminars.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to monitor the utilisation of this Grant by individual TCMPs to defray the cost of attending CPE courses and make adjustments if necessary.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Prof Fatimah Lateef rightly pointed out, TCMPs can also make claims under SkillsFuture funding for their courses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to encourage CPE course providers to get their courses accredited by SkillsFuture Singapore so that more TCMPs can benefit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef also asked whether there could be some flexibility given to the TCMPs during the first two years of implementation of compulsory CPE.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, the TCMPs should be familiar with the CPE framework and guidelines on points accumulation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For new registered TCMPs, they will be issued PCs valid until June 2020 and will be required to accumulate 50 CPE points in order to renew their PCs in June 2022.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, they start accumulating points after June 2020 and then, in June 2022, they will be required to have the requisite 50 CPE points for the PC renewal.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Of the 2,800 existing TCMPs holding valid PCs, half of them will have their PCs expiring in June this year and the other half in June next year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For those with PCs expiring in June this year, their PCs will be renewed until June 2020.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This exercise is to align the existing cohort so that the CPE requirement can start at the same time for all existing TCMPs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Between now till June 2020, the Board will engage the TCMPs and CPE course providers to update them on the revised CPE assessment framework.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We strongly urge all TCMPs to actively participate in CPE and familiarise themselves with the online CPE system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked how TCMPs who are not currently in active practice will be impacted with the passing of this Bill.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the CPE requirement is uniformly applied to all TCMPs who wish to practise, those who do not currently hold a valid PC will have to fulfil the CPE points requirement before they can apply to resume their practice.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu also asked how MOH will ensure the availability and quality of accredited CPE courses upon the implementation of compulsory CPE.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the availability of CPE courses, the Board has been engaging the course providers to organise more courses in anticipation of the implementation of compulsory CPE.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To further ensure that there are adequate courses, the CPE course providers will be required to fulfil a minimum number of course-hours per year to maintain their accreditation status.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Board has established guidelines for the accreditation of CPE providers and courses, such as the credentials of the speakers or instructors, to ensure that they are of an acceptable standard.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef may be pleased to note that with the online CPE system, TCMPs may log on via the Board's website to search for CPE activities they wish to attend and monitor their CPE points.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The system will be enhanced to send reminders at appropriate junctures to TCMPs who are at risk of not satisfying their CPE points requirement to help them fulfil these requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We note Mr Gan Thiam Poh's suggestion to integrate records of patients receiving treatment from both mainstream and TCM service providers for more coordinated management of care.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, as TCM is complementary to mainstream treatment and there are clinical and technical challenges that make it difficult to integrate the records, we will continue to work with the TCM community in order to provide a holistic approach towards patient management through other avenues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, the TCM Development Grant supports the TCM service providers to strengthen their operating capabilities, including the adoption of information technology (IT) solutions and enhancement of clinic facilities for TCM clinics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for information on the number of complaints received, disciplinary action taken and the trend over the years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The number of complaints received by the Board each year since 2013 has remained relatively constant at less than 10 per year, with about half of these cases requiring disciplinary action against the TCMPs involved.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The cases can be broadly categorised into professional misconduct, negligence, use of western medicines and criminal conviction.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The actions the Board can take against a TCMP is dependent on the gravity of the matter the TCMP is guilty of and range from issuing a letter of advice, censure or the suspension or cancellation of registration.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While the number of cases is relatively low, we need to continue to ensure that the disciplinary framework remains relevant and effective in safeguarding public interest and safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will be effected through the proposed three-pronged approach mentioned in my opening speech, namely, to enhance the disciplinary framework to improve efficiency, increase maximum financial penalty to provide sufficient deterrence and enhance investigative powers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This quantum is similar to the maximum financial penalty applicable for dentists, pharmacists and allied health professionals in the Dental Registration Act, Pharmacists Registration Act and Allied Health Professions Act, but lower than the maximum penalty of $100,000 for doctors under the Medical Registration Act (MRA).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have, on balance, decided on the $50,000 maximum quantum as TCMPs provide direct outpatient care to patients, similar to the allied health professionals and dentists in general.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To Mr Louis Ng's query on whether the Board informs the complainant of the findings of the inquiry and if it communicates with former patients of the TCMP if the TCMP is found guilty of misconduct, the Board will promptly inform both the complainant and TCMP involved of the Board's findings and decisions in writing once the inquiry process has been completed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Furthermore, upon the conclusion of the case, a press release will typically be issued and published on the Board's website for public access.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Board has put in place a sentencing framework based on the degree of harm and culpability to assess the seriousness of the offence and to guide the appropriate sentencing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As deemed necessary, the Board will update the framework.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, the Board also engages the Academy of Chinese Medicine Singapore for expert advice on TCM professional matters.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef and Dr Chia Shi-Lu commented on the representation of the Board.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We agree that the Board should consist of experienced and well-versed TCMPs who are conversant with various aspects of TCM practice.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, the current composition of the Board requires Board members who are TCMPs to have at least 10 years' experience in the practice of TCM.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We think this would suffice as, since its inception, the Board has comprised the maximum number of members allowed under the Act.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Louis Ng sought clarifications on the differences in the use of the term "mental or physical disability" in section 6 of the Act which sets out the criteria for disqualification of Board members and "mental or physical condition" in section 19 of the amended Act, which allows the Board to take certain action against the TCMP concerned.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will better safeguard patients' interests as the TCMPs are directly responsible for the care of their patients.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the other hand, we recognise that a person may still be able to contribute effectively as a member of the Board even if he was afflicted by a mental or physical condition, like a mild stroke, that does not affect his daily activities and mental capacity.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, this same condition may affect a practising TCMP's ability to provide safe and effective care.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Inquiry Committee for conducting a health inquiry relating to a TCMP's fitness to practise should consist of members who have the relevant expertise to inquire into the matter of which it is appointed, for example, a member who is a medical practitioner in a relevant field.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Mr Chen Show Mao may also like to note that MOH regularly reviews the regulations and policies on TCM, taking into consideration the advancements in medical science and evolving standards of TCM.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, based on the latest literature on safety of use, MOH has lifted the ban on raw herbs containing berberine (黄连), to allow practitioners more options in the use of TCM in their practice and service to the public.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since 2005, acupuncture has also been allowed in our public hospitals.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also happy to note that the research project, supported by the TCM Research Grant, on dry eyes undertaken by the Singapore Eye Research Institute and Singapore Chung Hwa Medical Institution, has shown encouraging results.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We hope that this will foster greater research collaborations between Western Medicine and TCM.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the possible standardisation of charges for TCM services and recognition of MCs issued by TCMPs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As TCM plays a complementary role to mainstream medicine in Singapore's healthcare system, MOH will leave it to the employers and companies to decide if they wish to recognise the MCs issued by TCMPs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef also pointed out that there is a range of charges for TCM services.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is due to a correspondingly diverse range of TCM practices and services offered, from charity TCM clinics operated by Voluntary Welfare Organisations to large industry players with chain clinics, catering to all segments of the population.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, the charges will continue to be left to market forces.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There has been a decline in the use of Chinese herbs which are mainly available from Chinese medical halls, compared to the use of Chinese Proprietary Medicines, that is, Chinese medicines in the prepared form, due to the latter's convenience and ease of use.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding this, MOH supports the continuing education of herbal dispensers as part of the upskilling of the TCM industry.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Herbal dispensers listed with the Board are also eligible for funding support provided under the Development Grant.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: MOH will continue to support and promote the professionalism of TCMPs and ensure consistency and safety of TCM use.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are, indeed, heartened by the support of the TCM community and the public during our consultation and engagement sessions, as well as the support of Members of this House.
